translations.idiomatic: Rites 15

translations.literal: (Auspicious Rites Three)〉
translations.idiomatic: Auspicious Rites 3)

sentences.zh: ○聖節諸慶節

translations.literal: ○ Imperial Birthday and Various Celebratory Festivals
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Birthday and Other Celebratory Festivals

sentences.zh: 聖節。

translations.literal: Imperial birthday.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Birthday

sentences.zh: 建隆元年，群臣請以二月十六日為長春節。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianlong, the assembled ministers requested that the sixteenth day of the second month be made the Changchun Festival.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 1 (960), the ministers asked that the emperor's birthday on the sixteenth day of the second month be established as the Changchun Festival.

sentences.zh: 正月十七日，於大相國寺建道場以祝壽，至日，上壽退，百僚詣寺行香。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth day of the first month, a ritual arena was established at the Great Xiangguo Monastery to pray for long life; on the day itself, after the birthday salutation the emperor withdrew, and the hundred officials went to the monastery to offer incense.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth day of the first month, a longevity ritual was opened at the Great Xiangguo Monastery; when the day came, the emperor withdrew after receiving birthday felicitations, and all officials went to the monastery to burn incense.

sentences.zh: 尋詔：“今後長春節及諸慶節，常參官、致仕官、僧道、百姓等毋得進奉。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter an edict stated: "Henceforth, for the Changchun Festival and all other celebratory festivals, regularly attending officials, retired officials, monks and Daoists, and commoners alike must not present tribute offerings.
translations.idiomatic: An edict soon followed: "From now on, at the Changchun Festival and other celebratory festivals, officials on regular attendance, retired officials, clergy, and the common people must not present tribute offerings.

sentences.zh: 太宗以十月七日為乾明節，復改為壽寧節。

translations.literal: Taizong took the seventh day of the tenth month as the Qianming Festival, which was later changed to the Shouning Festival.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's birthday was first observed as the Qianming Festival on the seventh day of the tenth month, then renamed the Shouning Festival.

sentences.zh: 真宗以十二月二日為承天節。

translations.literal: Zhenzong took the second day of the twelfth month as the Chengtian Festival.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong's birthday was established as the Chengtian Festival on the second day of the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 其儀：帝御長春殿，諸王上壽，次樞密使副、宣徽、三司使，次使相，次管軍節度使、兩使留後、觀察使，次節度使至觀察使，次皇 親任觀察使以下，各上壽，仍以金酒器、銀香合、馬、袖表為獻。

translations.literal: The ritual: the emperor took his seat in the Changchun Hall; the princes offered birthday felicitations first, next the vice commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs, the commissioners of the Palace and Inner Service, and the commissioners of the Three Departments, next the commissioners with ministerial rank, next the military commissioners in charge of armies, the two commissioners with acting status, and the observation commissioners, next from military commissioners down to observation commissioners, next imperial clansmen holding observation commissioner rank and below—each offered birthday felicitations, and also presented gold wine vessels, silver incense boxes, horses, and sleeve memorials as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The procedure was as follows: the emperor presided in the Changchun Hall. Princes offered birthday felicitations first, followed in order by the vice commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs, the commissioners of the Palace and Inner Service, and the Three Departments; then commissioners with ministerial rank; then army commanders, acting commissioners, and observation commissioners; then military commissioners through observation commissioners; then imperial clansmen of observation commissioner rank and below. Each group offered felicitations and presented gold wine vessels, silver incense boxes, horses, and sleeve memorials.

sentences.zh: 既畢，鹹赴崇德殿敘班，宰相率百官上壽，賜酒三行，皆用教坊樂，賜衣一襲，文武群臣、方鎮州 軍皆有貢禮。

translations.literal: When this was finished, all went to the Chongde Hall to take their places in order; the chief minister led the hundred officials in offering birthday felicitations; wine was bestowed in three rounds, all with music from the Court Entertainment Office; one suit of clothing was granted; civil and military officials and the regional commands all had tribute gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward everyone assembled in the Chongde Hall in proper order. The chief minister led the officials in offering birthday felicitations. The court granted three rounds of wine with Court Entertainment Office music and one suit of clothing; civil and military officials and the regional commands all presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 前一月，百官、內職、牧伯各就佛寺修齋祝壽，罷日以香賜之，仍各設會，賜上尊酒及諸果，百官兼賜教坊樂。

translations.literal: One month beforehand, officials, inner-service personnel, and regional governors each held vegetarian fasts at Buddhist monasteries to pray for long life; on the day the fast ended incense was bestowed on them; they also each held gatherings, and superior wine and various fruits were granted; officials additionally received Court Entertainment Office music.
translations.idiomatic: A month in advance, officials, inner-service staff, and regional governors observed vegetarian fasts at Buddhist temples to pray for the emperor's long life. When the fast ended, they received incense as a gift and held banquets at which fine wine and fruit were served; officials also received music from the Court Entertainment Office.

sentences.zh: 景德二年，始令樞密三司使副、學士復赴百官齋會，少卿、監、刺史以上及近職一子賜恩，僧道則賜紫衣、師號，禁屠，輟刑。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingde, it was first ordered that vice commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs and the Three Departments and academicians again attend the officials' vegetarian gatherings; junior ministers, supervisors, and prefects and above, together with one son of a close attendant, received grace; monks and Daoists were granted purple robes and honorific titles; slaughter was forbidden and punishments suspended.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde 2 (1005), vice commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs and the Three Departments and Hanlin academicians were again required to attend the officials' fasting banquets. Junior ministers, supervisors, and prefects and above, plus one son of each close attendant, received imperial favor. Monks and Daoists received purple robes and honorific titles, slaughter was banned, and executions were suspended.

sentences.zh: 仁宗以四月十四日為乾元節，正月八日皇太后為長寧節。

translations.literal: Renzong took the fourteenth day of the fourth month as the Qianyuan Festival, and the eighth day of the first month for the Empress Dowager as the Changning Festival.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong's birthday was the Qianyuan Festival on the fourteenth day of the fourth month; the Empress Dowager's was the Changning Festival on the eighth day of the first month.

sentences.zh: 詔定長寧節上壽儀：太后垂簾崇政殿，百官及契丹使班庭下，宰臣以下進奉上壽，閣門使於殿上簾外立 侍，百官再拜，宰臣升殿，跪進酒簾外，內臣跪承以入。

translations.literal: An edict fixed the Changning Festival birthday ritual: the Empress Dowager held court behind the curtain in the Chongzheng Hall; officials and the Khitan envoy stood in formation in the courtyard; the chief ministers and below presented birthday felicitations; the gate commissioners stood in attendance outside the curtain on the hall; the hundred officials bowed twice; the chief minister ascended the hall, knelt, and presented wine outside the curtain; inner attendants knelt to receive it and carry it in.
translations.idiomatic: An edict prescribed the Changning birthday ceremony: the Empress Dowager held audience behind a curtain in the Chongzheng Hall while officials and the Khitan envoy stood in the courtyard. Chief ministers and below presented birthday felicitations. Gate commissioners waited outside the curtain on the dais. Officials bowed twice; the chief minister ascended, knelt, and offered wine at the curtain; inner attendants knelt to receive it and carry it inside.

sentences.zh: 宰臣奏曰：“長寧節，臣等不勝歡抃，謹上千萬歲壽。

translations.literal: The chief minister memorialized: "On the Changning Festival, your servants cannot contain their joy and respectfully offer felicitations for ten thousand myriad years of life.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister reported: "On the Changning Festival, we cannot contain our joy and respectfully wish Your Majesty ten thousand myriad years of life.

sentences.zh: ”復降，再拜，三稱萬歲。

translations.literal: " He descended again, bowed twice, and thrice shouted "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: " He withdrew, bowed twice, and thrice shouted "Long live the Empress!"

sentences.zh: 內臣承旨宣曰：“得公等 壽酒，與公等同喜。

translations.literal: An inner attendant, receiving the imperial order, announced: "Having received your birthday wine, I share your joy with you.
translations.idiomatic: An inner attendant, conveying the imperial response, announced: "Having received your birthday wine, I share this joy with you.

sentences.zh: ”鹹再拜。

translations.literal: " All bowed again.
translations.idiomatic: " Everyone bowed again.

sentences.zh: 宰臣升殿，內侍出簾外跪授虛盞，宰臣跪受，降，再拜舞蹈，三稱萬歲。

translations.literal: The chief minister ascended the hall; an inner attendant came out, knelt outside the curtain, and handed over an empty cup; the chief minister knelt to receive it, descended, bowed twice, performed the dance obeisance, and thrice shouted "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister ascended again. An inner attendant knelt outside the curtain and handed over an empty cup; the chief minister knelt to receive it, withdrew, bowed twice, performed the dance obeisance, and thrice shouted "Long live the Empress!"

sentences.zh: 內侍承旨宣群臣升殿，再拜，升，陳進奉物當殿庭，通事舍 人稱“宰臣以下進奉”，客省使殿上喝“進奉出”。

translations.literal: An inner attendant, receiving the imperial order, announced that the assembled ministers should ascend the hall; they bowed twice, ascended, and displayed tribute offerings in the central courtyard; the relay secretary called out "The chief ministers and below present tribute"; the guest-reception commissioner on the hall shouted "Tribute withdrawn."
translations.idiomatic: An inner attendant announced that the ministers should ascend. They bowed twice, went up, and displayed tribute in the central courtyard. The relay secretary called "Tribute from the chief ministers and below"; the guest-reception commissioner on the dais called "Withdraw the tribute."

sentences.zh: 內謁者監進第二盞，賜酒三行，侍中奏禮畢，皆再拜舞蹈。

translations.literal: The inner usher director presented the second cup; wine was granted in three rounds; the attendant-in-chief reported that the rites were complete; all bowed twice and performed the dance obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: The inner usher director presented the second cup. Three rounds of wine were granted. When the attendant-in-chief reported that the rites were finished, everyone bowed twice and performed the dance obeisance.

sentences.zh: 太后還內，百官詣內東門拜表稱賀。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager returned within; officials went to the inner east gate to present congratulatory memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager withdrew to the inner quarters; officials went to the inner east gate to present congratulatory memorials.

sentences.zh: 其外命婦舊入內 者即入內上壽，不入內者進表。

translations.literal: As for outer consorts who had formerly entered the palace, they now entered to offer birthday felicitations; those who did not enter presented memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Outer consorts who had previously been admitted to the palace entered to offer birthday felicitations; those not admitted submitted memorials instead.

sentences.zh: 內侍引內命婦上壽，次引外命婦，如百官儀。

translations.literal: Inner attendants led inner consorts to offer birthday felicitations, then led outer consorts, following the same ritual as the officials.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants led inner consorts to offer birthday felicitations, then outer consorts, following the officials' procedure.

sentences.zh: 次日大宴。

translations.literal: On the following day a great banquet was held.
translations.idiomatic: A grand banquet was held the next day.

sentences.zh: 英宗以正月三日為壽聖節。

translations.literal: Yingzong took the third day of the first month as the Shousheng Festival.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong's birthday was established as the Shousheng Festival on the third day of the first month.

sentences.zh: 禮官奏：“故事，聖節上壽，親王、樞密於長春殿，宰臣、百官於崇德殿，天聖諒沍皆於崇政殿。

translations.literal: The ritual officials memorialized: "By precedent, for imperial birthday felicitations princes and the Bureau of Military Affairs were at the Changchun Hall, chief ministers and officials at the Chongde Hall; during the Tiansheng mourning all were at the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officials reported: "By precedent, birthday felicitations for the emperor had princes and the Bureau of Military Affairs in the Changchun Hall and chief ministers and officials in the Chongde Hall; during the Tiansheng mourning period everyone used the Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: ”於是紫宸上壽，群臣升殿間，飲獻一觴而退。

translations.literal: " Thereupon birthday felicitations were held in the Zichen Hall; as ministers ascended the hall they drank and presented one cup and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " Birthday felicitations were therefore held in the Zichen Hall; ministers ascended in turn, drank, presented one cup, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 又一日，賜宴於錫慶院。

translations.literal: On another day a banquet was granted at the Xiqing Court.
translations.idiomatic: On another day a banquet was granted at the Xiqing Court.

sentences.zh: 神宗以熙寧元年四月十日為同天節，以宅憂罷上壽，惟拜表稱賀。

translations.literal: Shenzong took the tenth day of the fourth month in the first year of Xining as the Tongtian Festival; because he was in mourning at home, birthday felicitations were suspended and only memorials of congratulation were offered.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 1 (1068), Shenzong's birthday on the tenth day of the fourth month became the Tongtian Festival. While he was in mourning for his father, birthday felicitations were suspended and officials offered congratulatory memorials only.

sentences.zh: 明年，親王、樞密使、管軍、駙馬、諸司使副詣垂拱殿，宰臣、百官、大國使詣紫宸殿上壽，命坐，賜酒三行，不舉樂。

translations.literal: The next year princes, the commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, army commanders, imperial sons-in-law, and vice commissioners of the various offices went to the Chui'gong Hall; chief ministers, officials, and envoys of great states went to the Zichen Hall to offer birthday felicitations; they were ordered to sit; wine was granted in three rounds; music was not performed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year princes, the Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner, army commanders, imperial sons-in-law, and vice commissioners of the various offices went to the Chui'gong Hall, while chief ministers, officials, and envoys of great states offered birthday felicitations in the Zichen Hall. They were seated and granted three rounds of wine without music.

sentences.zh: 明年，以大旱，罷同天節上壽，群臣赴東上閣門表賀。

translations.literal: The next year, because of severe drought, Tongtian Festival birthday felicitations were suspended; ministers went to the eastern upper Gate Office to present congratulatory memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, because of severe drought, Tongtian Festival birthday felicitations were canceled; ministers presented congratulatory memorials at the eastern upper Gate Office.

sentences.zh: 中書門下言：“同天節上壽班，自今樞密使副、宣徽、三司使、殿前馬步軍副都指揮使以上共作一班，進酒一盞；

translations.literal: The Secretariat and Chancellery stated: "For the Tongtian Festival birthday formation, from now on the vice commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs, the commissioners of the Palace and Inner Service and the Three Departments, and the vice commanders-in-chief of the Palace and Horse Armies and above shall form one formation together and present one cup of wine;
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat and Chancellery reported: "For Tongtian Festival birthday formations, henceforth the vice commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs, the commissioners of the Palace and Inner Service and the Three Departments, and the vice commanders-in-chief of the Palace and Horse Armies and above shall form a single formation and present one cup of wine together.

sentences.zh: 親王、宗室、使相至觀察、駙馬、管軍觀察使以 上，皆赴紫宸殿，依本班序立上壽，更不赴垂拱殿。

translations.literal: princes, imperial clansmen, commissioners with ministerial rank down to observation commissioners, imperial sons-in-law, and army observation commissioners and above shall all go to the Zichen Hall, stand in birthday formation according to their original ranks, and no longer go to the Chui'gong Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Princes, imperial clansmen, commissioners with ministerial rank through observation commissioners, imperial sons-in-law, and army observation commissioners and above shall all go to the Zichen Hall, stand in birthday formation by their usual ranks, and no longer attend the Chui'gong Hall.

sentences.zh: ”蓋以管軍觀察使以上及親王、駙馬並於垂拱殿以官序高下各班進酒畢而日晏，外朝有班者仍詣紫宸殿，議者以 為近瀆，改焉。

translations.literal: " This was because army observation commissioners and above together with princes and imperial sons-in-law all presented wine in separate formations at the Chui'gong Hall according to rank from high to low, and by the time they finished it was late in the day; those with formations in the outer court still had to go to the Zichen Hall; critics regarded this as nearly irreverent, and it was changed.
translations.idiomatic: " The change was made because army observation commissioners and above, together with princes and imperial sons-in-law, had each presented wine in separate rank-ordered formations at the Chui'gong Hall until evening, after which outer-court officials still had to proceed to the Zichen Hall—critics considered this nearly irreverent.

sentences.zh: 而詔袒免以上宗婦聽班賀於禁中。

translations.literal: An edict also allowed imperial clanswomen of the fifth mourning degree and above to attend formation and offer congratulations within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also allowed imperial clanswomen of the fifth mourning degree and above to join formation and offer congratulations within the palace.

sentences.zh: 哲宗即位，詔以太皇太后七月十六日為坤成節。

translations.literal: When Zhezong took the throne, an edict established the sixteenth day of the seventh month for the Grand Empress Dowager as the Kuncheng Festival.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong ascended the throne, an edict established the Grand Empress Dowager's birthday as the Kuncheng Festival on the sixteenth day of the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 宰臣請以十二月八日為興龍節。

translations.literal: The chief ministers requested that the eighth day of the twelfth month be made the Xinglong Festival.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers asked that the eighth day of the twelfth month be established as the Xinglong Festival.

sentences.zh: 哲宗本七日生，以避僖祖忌，故後一日。

translations.literal: Zhezong was originally born on the seventh day; to avoid the taboo day of Emperor Xizu, it was moved to the following day.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezong was actually born on the seventh day, but the observance was moved one day later to avoid the taboo anniversary of Emperor Xizu.

sentences.zh: 徽宗以十月十日為天寧節，定上壽儀：皇帝御垂拱殿，群臣通班起居畢，分班，從義郎以下醫官、待詔等先退。

translations.literal: Huizong took the tenth day of the tenth month as the Tianning Festival and fixed the birthday ritual: the emperor presided in the Chui'gong Hall; after the assembled ministers had made their general salutation and withdrawn into formation, medical officers, awaiting-edict officials, and the like below the rank of gentleman for meritorious service withdrew first.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong's birthday became the Tianning Festival on the tenth day of the tenth month. The birthday ritual was fixed as follows: the emperor presided in the Chui'gong Hall. After the assembled ministers completed their general salutation and formed ranks, medical officers, awaiting-edict officials, and those below gentleman for meritorious service withdrew first.

sentences.zh: 知引進司官一員讀奏目，知東上閣門官一員奏進壽 酒，由東階升，舍人通教坊使以下讚再拜，奏聖躬萬福，又再拜，復位。

translations.literal: One official of the Reception Directorate read the memorial list; one eastern upper Gate Office official reported the presentation of birthday wine; he ascended by the eastern steps; the usher had those below the Court Entertainment Office commissioner call out and bow twice; they reported the emperor's ten thousand blessings of body; bowed twice again; and returned to place.
translations.idiomatic: An official of the Reception Directorate read the memorial list. An eastern upper Gate Office official reported the presentation of birthday wine and ascended by the eastern steps. The usher had those below the Court Entertainment Office commissioner bow twice, report the emperor's ten thousand blessings of body, bow twice again, and return to position.

sentences.zh: 次看盞人稍前，舍人讚再拜，讚上殿祗候，分東西兩階立，俟進酒升殿。

translations.literal: Next the cup-inspector advanced slightly; the usher called for two bows; called for attendance on the hall; they stood on the eastern and western steps divided, waiting for the wine presentation to ascend the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Next the cup-inspector advanced slightly. The usher called for two bows, then for attendance on the hall. Attendants divided between the eastern and western steps and waited for the wine presentation to ascend.

sentences.zh: 次舍人引親王入殿 庭，北向立，讚再拜，班首奏萬福。

translations.literal: Next the usher led the princes into the hall courtyard, standing facing north; called for two bows; the formation leader reported ten thousand blessings.
translations.idiomatic: Next the usher led the princes into the hall courtyard to stand facing north, called for two bows, and the formation leader reported ten thousand blessings.

sentences.zh: 舍人引進奉西入，列於親王後，酒器簷床置馬前，揖天武躬奏萬福，進奉馬先出。

translations.literal: The usher led tribute offerings in from the west, arrayed behind the princes; wine vessels on the eave couch were placed before the horses; the Tianwu guards bowed and reported ten thousand blessings; the tribute horses went out first.
translations.idiomatic: The usher led tribute offerings in from the west and arrayed them behind the princes. Wine vessels on the eave couch were set before the horses. The Tianwu guards bowed and reported ten thousand blessings, and the tribute horses were led out first.

sentences.zh: 內侍進禦茶床，殿中監酹酒訖，知東上閣門官 殿上躬奏：“親王某以下進壽酒。

translations.literal: Inner attendants brought forward the imperial tea couch; the director of the palace service libated the wine; the eastern upper Gate Office official on the hall bowed and reported: "Prince So-and-so and below present birthday wine.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants brought forward the imperial tea couch. The director of the palace service libated the wine. The eastern upper Gate Office official on the dais bowed and reported: "Prince So-and-so and below present birthday wine.

sentences.zh: ”舍人揖親王以下躬讚再拜，乃引親王二員升殿，知東上閣門官引詣御坐前，舍人東階下西向立，

translations.literal: " The usher had the princes and below bow; called for two bows; then led two princes up the hall; the eastern upper Gate Office official led them before the imperial seat; the usher stood on the eastern steps below facing west,
translations.idiomatic: " The usher had the princes and below bow and called for two bows, then led two princes up the hall. The eastern upper Gate Office official led them before the imperial seat while the usher stood on the eastern steps below facing west.

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket.

sentences.zh: （後準此。）〉

translations.literal: (Hereafter follow this.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Hereafter follow this precedent.)

sentences.zh: 尚醞典禦奉槃、盞 授班首，搢笏受盤、盞，西向立，奉禦啟盞，親王一員搢笏注酒，班首奉詣御坐東進訖，少退，虛跪，興，以槃授典禦，退，閣門引降階。

translations.literal: The imperial brew master presented tray and cup to the formation leader; he inserted his tablet, received tray and cup, stood facing west; the imperial attendant opened the cup; one prince inserted his tablet and poured wine; the formation leader bore it east of the imperial seat and presented it; when finished he withdrew slightly, knelt in empty obeisance, rose, handed the tray to the brew master, withdrew, and the Gate Office led him down the steps.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial brew master presented tray and cup to the formation leader, who inserted his tablet, received them, and stood facing west. The imperial attendant opened the cup; one prince inserted his tablet and poured the wine. The formation leader bore it east of the imperial seat and presented it, then withdrew slightly, performed an empty kneeling obeisance, rose, handed the tray to the brew master, withdrew, and the Gate Office led him down the steps.

sentences.zh: 舍人引當殿北向立，東 上，讚拜，興，搢笏跪奉表，舍人接表，一員在東，餘詣親王西，置表笏上，授引進。

translations.literal: The usher led those on duty in the hall to stand facing north, advancing east; called for bowing, rising, inserting tablet, kneeling to present the memorial; the usher received the memorial; one stood on the east, the rest went west of the princes, placed the memorial on the tablet, and handed it to the reception official.
translations.idiomatic: The usher led those on duty in the hall to stand facing north and advance east. He called for bowing, rising, inserting the tablet, and kneeling to present the memorial. The usher received the memorial; one stood on the east while the rest went west of the princes, placed the memorial on the tablet, and handed it to the reception official.

sentences.zh: 知引進司官殿上讀奏目，退，親王以下俯伏，興，躬，舍人讚再拜，引班首升 東階，餘殿下分立。

translations.literal: The Reception Directorate official read the memorial list on the hall and withdrew; the princes and below prostrated themselves, rose, bowed; the usher called for two bows and led the formation leader up the eastern steps while the rest stood divided below the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Reception Directorate official read the memorial list on the dais and withdrew. The princes and below prostrated themselves, rose, and bowed. The usher called for two bows and led the formation leader up the eastern steps while the rest stood divided below.

sentences.zh: 閣門引詣御坐東，北向搢笏，尚醞典禦如前奉盤立，樂作，皇帝飲訖，受盞，復位，再拜如上儀。

translations.literal: The Gate Office led them east of the imperial seat; facing north they inserted their tablets; the imperial brew master presented the tray as before and stood; music sounded; when the emperor finished drinking he received the cup, returned to place, and bowed twice as in the ritual above.
translations.idiomatic: The Gate Office led them east of the imperial seat. Facing north they inserted their tablets while the imperial brew master presented the tray as before. Music sounded. When the emperor finished drinking, he received the cup, returned to position, and bowed twice as above.

sentences.zh: 知引進司官詣折檻東，西向宣曰“進奉收”。

translations.literal: The Reception Directorate official went to the east of the balustrade, faced west, and announced "Tribute received."
translations.idiomatic: The Reception Directorate official went east of the balustrade, faced west, and announced "Tribute received."

sentences.zh: 讚拜，舞蹈，又再拜，西出。

translations.literal: Called for bowing, dance obeisance, two bows again, and exit to the west.
translations.idiomatic: He called for bowing and the dance obeisance, then two more bows, and they exited to the west.

sentences.zh: 親王以下赴紫宸殿立班。

translations.literal: The princes and below went to the Zichen Hall to form ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The princes and below went to the Zichen Hall to form ranks.

sentences.zh: 引進官宣“進奉出”，天武奉進奉以出。

translations.literal: The reception commissioner announced "Tribute withdrawn"; the Tianwu guards bore the tribute out.
translations.idiomatic: The reception commissioner announced "Tribute withdrawn," and the Tianwu guards bore the tribute out.

sentences.zh: 閣門復立殿上，教坊使讚送禦酒，又再拜，教坊致語訖，讚再拜， 退。

translations.literal: The Gate Office again stood on the hall; the Court Entertainment Office commissioner called for presenting the imperial wine; bowed twice again; when the Court Entertainment Office address was finished, called for two bows and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Gate Office again stood on the dais. The Court Entertainment Office commissioner called for presenting the imperial wine; they bowed twice again. When the Court Entertainment address was finished, he called for two bows and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 次樞密官上壽，次管軍觀察以上上壽、進奉並如儀。

translations.literal: Next Bureau of Military Affairs officials offered birthday felicitations; next army observation commissioners and above offered birthday felicitations and tribute, all following the ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Next Bureau of Military Affairs officials offered birthday felicitations; next army observation commissioners and above offered felicitations and tribute, all following the same ritual.

sentences.zh: 內侍舉禦茶床，舍人讚教坊使以下謝祗應，再拜訖，閣門側奏無公事。

translations.literal: Inner attendants raised the imperial tea couch; the usher had those below the Court Entertainment Office commissioner thank them for attending; when the bows were finished, the Gate Office reported from the side that there was no official business.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants raised the imperial tea couch. The usher had those below the Court Entertainment Office commissioner thank the court for attending. When the bows were finished, the Gate Office reported from the side that there was no official business.

sentences.zh: 皇帝赴紫宸殿後閣受群 臣上壽。

translations.literal: The emperor went to the rear chamber of the Zichen Hall to receive birthday felicitations from the assembled ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to the rear chamber of the Zichen Hall to receive birthday felicitations from the assembled ministers.

sentences.zh: 質明，三公以下百僚並於殿門外就次，東上閣門、御史台、太常寺分引入詣殿庭東西立。

translations.literal: At daybreak, the three dukes and the hundred officials below all took their places outside the hall gates; the eastern upper Gate Office, the Censorate, and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices led them in separately to stand east and west in the hall courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak the three dukes and all officials below took their places outside the hall gates. The eastern upper Gate Office, the Censorate, and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices led them in separately to stand east and west in the hall courtyard.

sentences.zh: 閣門附內侍進班齊牌，皇帝出閣，禁衛諸班親從迎駕，自讚常起 居。

translations.literal: The Gate Office had inner attendants present the formation tally-board; the emperor came out of the chamber; the various guard formations and close attendants welcomed the imperial procession; they themselves called the regular salutation.
translations.idiomatic: The Gate Office had inner attendants present the formation tally-board. The emperor came out of the chamber. Guard formations and close attendants welcomed the procession and called the regular salutation themselves.

sentences.zh: 皇帝升坐，鳴鞭，禮直官、通事舍人引三公至執政官，御史台、東上閣門分引百官，並橫行北向立，典儀讚再拜舞蹈，班首奏萬福，又再拜訖，分東西立。

translations.literal: The emperor ascended and took his seat; the whip sounded; ritual officers and relay secretaries led the three dukes through the chief administrators; the Censorate and eastern upper Gate Office led the hundred officials separately; all stood in horizontal formation facing north; the master of ceremonies called for two bows and the dance obeisance; the formation leader reported ten thousand blessings; bowed twice again; then divided east and west.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ascended and took his seat; the whip sounded. Ritual officers and relay secretaries led the three dukes through the chief administrators; the Censorate and eastern upper Gate Office led the hundred officials separately. All stood in horizontal formation facing north. The master of ceremonies called for two bows and the dance obeisance. The formation leader reported ten thousand blessings, bowed twice again, then divided east and west.

sentences.zh: 禮直 官引殿中監、少監升東階，詣酒尊所稍西，南向西上立，舍人揖教坊使以下通班大起居，次看盞人謝升殿，讚再拜。

translations.literal: Ritual officers led the director and vice-director of the palace service up the eastern steps to the wine altar slightly west, standing south-facing and advancing west; the usher had those below the Court Entertainment Office commissioner make the great salutation in full formation; next the cup-inspector thanked for ascending the hall; called for two bows.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers led the director and vice-director of the palace service up the eastern steps to the wine altar slightly west, standing south-facing and advancing west. The usher had those below the Court Entertainment Office commissioner perform the great salutation in full formation. Next the cup-inspector thanked for ascending the hall and called for two bows.

sentences.zh: 內侍進禦茶床，殿侍酹酒訖，禮直官、通事舍人 分引三公至執政官，御史台、東上閣門分引百僚，並橫行北向立，典儀讚再拜，讚者承傳，在位官皆再拜。

translations.literal: Inner attendants brought forward the imperial tea couch; the palace attendant libated the wine; ritual officers and relay secretaries led the three dukes through the chief administrators; the Censorate and eastern upper Gate Office led the hundred officials separately; all stood in horizontal formation facing north; the master of ceremonies called for two bows; the caller transmitted; all officials in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants brought forward the imperial tea couch. The palace attendant libated the wine. Ritual officers and relay secretaries again led the three dukes through the chief administrators while the Censorate and eastern upper Gate Office led the hundred officials separately. All stood in horizontal formation facing north. The master of ceremonies called for two bows; the caller transmitted the call; every official in attendance bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 禮直官、通事舍人引上公升東階，東上閣門官接引升殿， 授盞、啟盞如上儀。

translations.literal: Ritual officers and relay secretaries led the senior duke up the eastern steps; the eastern upper Gate Office official led him up the hall; presenting and opening the cup followed the ritual above.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers and relay secretaries led the senior duke up the eastern steps. The eastern upper Gate Office official led him onto the hall. Presenting and opening the cup followed the ritual above.

sentences.zh: 上公詣御坐，俯伏跪奏：“文武百僚、上公具官臣某等稽首言：天寧令節，臣等不勝大慶，謹上千萬歲壽。

translations.literal: The senior duke went before the imperial seat, prostrated himself kneeling, and reported: "The civil and military officials, the senior duke with full title, your servant and others bow our heads and say: On the Tianning command festival, your servants cannot contain our great rejoicing and respectfully offer ten thousand myriad years of life.
translations.idiomatic: The senior duke went before the imperial seat, prostrated himself kneeling, and reported: "The civil and military officials, the senior duke with full title, your servant and others bow our heads and say: On the Tianning command festival we cannot contain our great rejoicing and respectfully wish Your Majesty ten thousand myriad years of life.

sentences.zh: ”俯伏，興，退，降階，舍人接引復 位，典儀讚再拜訖，禮直官引知樞密院官詣御坐前承旨，退詣折檻稍東，西向宣曰：“得公等壽酒，與公等內外同慶。

translations.literal: " Prostrating himself, rising, withdrawing, descending the steps, the usher leading him back to place; when the master of ceremonies called for two bows, ritual officers led the Bureau of Military Affairs official before the imperial seat to receive the order, withdrew to slightly east of the balustrade, faced west, and announced: "Having received your birthday wine, I share this joy inside and outside with you.
translations.idiomatic: " He prostrated himself, rose, withdrew, and descended the steps while the usher led him back to position. When the master of ceremonies called for two bows, ritual officers led the Bureau of Military Affairs official before the imperial seat to receive the order, withdrew to slightly east of the balustrade, faced west, and announced: "Having received your birthday wine, I share this joy with you within and without.

sentences.zh: ”典儀讚拜如儀，百官分東西立。

translations.literal: " The master of ceremonies called for bowing as in the ritual; officials divided east and west.
translations.idiomatic: " The master of ceremonies called for bowing as in the ritual, and officials divided east and west.

sentences.zh: 禮直官、通 事舍人引上公升東階，東上閣門官接引詣御坐東，搢笏，殿中監授盤，上公奉進御坐東，北向，樂作，皇帝飲訖，閣門引接盞，降，復位典儀讚拜如上儀。

translations.literal: Ritual officers and relay secretaries led the senior duke up the eastern steps; the eastern upper Gate Office official led him east of the imperial seat; he inserted his tablet; the director of the palace service presented the tray; the senior duke bore it east of the imperial seat facing north; music sounded; when the emperor finished drinking, the Gate Office led him to receive the cup, descend, and return to place; the master of ceremonies called for bowing as above.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers and relay secretaries led the senior duke up the eastern steps. The eastern upper Gate Office official led him east of the imperial seat. He inserted his tablet; the director of the palace service presented the tray; the senior duke bore it east of the imperial seat facing north. Music sounded. When the emperor finished drinking, the Gate Office led him to receive the cup, descend, and return to position; the master of ceremonies called for bowing as above.

sentences.zh: 宗室遙郡 以下先退。

translations.literal: Imperial clansmen of remote commanderies and below withdrew first.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen of remote commanderies and below withdrew first.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引樞密院官詣御坐前承旨，退詣折檻稍東，宣曰：“宣群臣升殿。

translations.literal: Ritual officers led the Bureau of Military Affairs official before the imperial seat to receive the order, withdrew to slightly east of the balustrade, and announced: "It is ordered that the assembled ministers ascend the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers led the Bureau of Military Affairs official before the imperial seat to receive the order, withdrew to slightly east of the balustrade, and announced: "It is ordered that the assembled ministers ascend the hall.

sentences.zh: ”典儀讚拜訖，禮直官、通事舍人分引三公以下升東階，親王、使相以下升西 階；

translations.literal: " When the master of ceremonies called for bowing, ritual officers and relay secretaries led the three dukes and below up the eastern steps, princes and commissioners with ministerial rank and below up the western steps;
translations.idiomatic: " When the master of ceremonies finished calling for bows, ritual officers and relay secretaries led the three dukes and below up the eastern steps and princes and commissioners with ministerial rank and below up the western steps.

sentences.zh: 御史台、東上閣門分引秘書監以下升兩朵殿，並東西廊席後立。

translations.literal: the Censorate and eastern upper Gate Office led those from the Directorate of the Palace Library and below up the two flower halls, all standing behind the east and west corridor seats.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate and eastern upper Gate Office led those from the Directorate of the Palace Library and below up the two flower halls, all standing behind the east and west corridor seats.

sentences.zh: 尚醞典禦以盞授殿中監，奉禦啟盞，殿中監西向立，殿中少監以酒注於盞，

translations.literal: The imperial brew master presented the cup to the director of the palace service; the imperial attendant opened the cup; the director stood facing west; the vice-director poured wine into the cup,
translations.idiomatic: The imperial brew master presented the cup to the director of the palace service. The imperial attendant opened the cup. The director stood facing west while the vice-director poured wine into the cup.

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket.

sentences.zh: （第二、第三準 此。）〉

translations.literal: (The second and third follow this.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The second and third rounds follow this procedure.)

sentences.zh: 奉詣御坐前，躬進訖，少退，奉盤西向立。

translations.literal: bore it before the imperial seat, bowed and presented it; withdrew slightly; stood facing west holding the tray.
translations.idiomatic: He bore it before the imperial seat, bowed and presented it, withdrew slightly, and stood facing west holding the tray.

sentences.zh: 樂作，皇帝飲訖，殿中監接盞退，授奉禦，出笏復位。

translations.literal: Music sounded; when the emperor finished drinking, the director of the palace service received the cup and withdrew, handing it to the imperial attendant; they removed their tablets and returned to place.
translations.idiomatic: Music sounded. When the emperor finished drinking, the director received the cup and withdrew, handing it to the imperial attendant; they removed their tablets and returned to position.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人分引殿上官橫行北向，舍人讚再拜，典儀曰“再拜 ”，讚者承傳，皆再拜。

translations.literal: Relay secretaries led officials on the hall in horizontal formation facing north; the usher called for two bows; the master of ceremonies said "Bow again"; the caller transmitted; all bowed again.
translations.idiomatic: Relay secretaries led officials on the hall into horizontal formation facing north. The usher called for two bows. The master of ceremonies said "Bow again"; the caller transmitted; everyone bowed again.

sentences.zh: 舍人讚就坐，各立席後，復讚就坐，群官皆坐。

translations.literal: The usher called to be seated; each stood behind his seat; called again to be seated; all officials sat.
translations.idiomatic: The usher called to be seated; each stood behind his seat; called again to be seated; and all officials sat.

sentences.zh: 酒初行，先宰臣，次百官，皆作樂。

translations.literal: When wine was first served, the chief ministers came first, then the hundred officials; music was performed throughout.
translations.idiomatic: When wine was first served, chief ministers came first, then the hundred officials, with music throughout.

sentences.zh: 尚食典禦、奉禦進食，太官設群官食，皇帝再舉酒，群 官興，立席後，樂作，飲訖，舍人讚就坐，再行群官酒，皇帝三舉酒，並如第二之儀。

translations.literal: The imperial food master and attendant presented food; the Imperial Kitchen set out food for the assembled officials; the emperor raised his cup a second time; the assembled officials rose, stood behind their seats; music sounded; when they finished drinking, the usher called to be seated; wine was served again to the assembled officials; the emperor raised his cup a third time, all following the ritual of the second round.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial food master and attendant presented food. The Imperial Kitchen set out food for the assembled officials. The emperor raised his cup a second time; officials rose and stood behind their seats while music played. When they finished drinking, the usher called them to sit. Wine was served again to the assembled officials. The emperor raised his cup a third time, all following the second-round procedure.

sentences.zh: 酒三行，舍人曰“可起”，群官興，立席後。

translations.literal: After three rounds of wine, the usher said "You may rise"; the assembled officials rose and stood behind their seats.
translations.idiomatic: After three rounds of wine the usher said "You may rise"; the assembled officials rose and stood behind their seats.

sentences.zh: 若宣示盞，即隨東上閣門官以下 揖，稱“宣示盞”，躬，讚就坐。

translations.literal: If an imperial cup was displayed, they followed the eastern upper Gate Office officials and below in bowing, saying "Imperial cup displayed," bowing, and the usher called to be seated.
translations.idiomatic: If an imperial cup was displayed, they followed the eastern upper Gate Office officials in bowing, saying "Imperial cup displayed," bowing, and sitting when the usher called.

sentences.zh: 若宣勸，即立席後，躬，飲訖，讚再拜。

translations.literal: If encouragement to drink was announced, they stood behind their seats, bowed, drank, and the usher called for two bows.
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor encouraged drinking, they stood behind their seats, bowed, drank, and the usher called for two bows.

sentences.zh: 內侍舉禦茶床，禮直官引左輔詣御坐前北向俯伏跪奏：“左輔具官臣某言禮畢。

translations.literal: Inner attendants raised the imperial tea couch; ritual officers led the left chief counselor before the imperial seat facing north, prostrating himself kneeling, and reported: "The left chief counselor with full title, your servant, reports that the rites are complete.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants raised the imperial tea couch. Ritual officers led the left chief counselor before the imperial seat facing north. He prostrated himself kneeling and reported: "The left chief counselor with full title, your servant, reports that the rites are complete.

sentences.zh: ”俯伏， 興，退，復位。

translations.literal: " Prostrating himself, rising, withdrawing, returning to place.
translations.idiomatic: " He prostrated himself, rose, withdrew, and returned to position.

sentences.zh: 禮直官、通事舍人分引三公以下文武百僚降階橫行北向立，樞密院官在親王後。

translations.literal: Ritual officers and relay secretaries led the three dukes and the civil and military hundred officials down the steps to stand in horizontal formation facing north; Bureau of Military Affairs officials stood behind the princes.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers and relay secretaries led the three dukes and civil and military officials down the steps to stand in horizontal formation facing north, with Bureau of Military Affairs officials behind the princes.

sentences.zh: 典儀讚再拜，皆舞蹈再拜退。

translations.literal: The master of ceremonies called for two bows; all performed the dance obeisance, bowed twice again, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The master of ceremonies called for two bows. All performed the dance obeisance, bowed twice again, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年四月十三日，太宰徐處仁等表請為乾龍節。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day of the fourth month in the first year of Jingkang, Grand Counselor Xu Churen and others memorialized requesting the Qianlong Festival.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth day of the fourth month in Jingkang 1 (1126), Grand Counselor Xu Churen and others memorialized asking that the emperor's birthday be established as the Qianlong Festival.

sentences.zh: 至日，皇帝帥百官詣龍德宮上壽畢，即本宮賜侍從官以上宴。

translations.literal: On the day, the emperor led the hundred officials to the Longde Palace to offer birthday felicitations; when finished, a banquet was granted at that palace to close attendants and above.
translations.idiomatic: On the day itself the emperor led the hundred officials to the Longde Palace to offer birthday felicitations. When that was finished, a banquet was granted at the palace to close attendants and above.

sentences.zh: 建炎元年五月，宰臣等上言，請以五月二十一日為天申節。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Jianyan, the chief ministers and others memorialized, requesting that the twenty-first day of the fifth month be made the Tianshen Festival.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Jianyan 1 (1127), the chief ministers memorialized asking that the twenty-first day of the fifth month be established as the Tianshen Festival.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：“朕承祖宗遺澤，獲托士民之上，求所以扶危持顛之道，未知攸濟。

translations.literal: The edict stated: "We have received the legacy grace of the ancestors and been placed above the scholars and commoners; we seek the way to support what is tottering and uphold what is falling, and do not yet know how to achieve it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "We have received our ancestors' legacy and been placed above the people. We seek how to steady what is tottering and save what is falling, and do not yet know the way.

sentences.zh: 念二聖鑾輿在遠，萬民失 業，將士暴露，夙夜痛悼，寢食幾廢，況以眇躬之故，聞樂飲酒，以自為樂乎？

translations.literal: Reflecting that the two emperors' imperial carriages are far away, the myriad people have lost their livelihoods, and soldiers lie exposed to the elements, we grieve day and night, our sleep and food nearly abandoned—how, for the sake of our slight person, could we hear music and drink wine to amuse ourselves?
translations.idiomatic: The two emperors remain captive far away, the people have lost their livelihoods, and soldiers lie exposed in the field. We grieve day and night and can scarcely eat or sleep. How could we, for our slight person alone, hear music and drink wine for our own pleasure?

sentences.zh: 非惟深拂朕誌，實增感於朕心。

translations.literal: This not only deeply goes against our will; it truly adds to the grief in our heart.
translations.idiomatic: That would not only deeply violate our intent; it would truly add to the grief in our heart.

sentences.zh: 所有將來天申節百官上壽常禮，可令寢罷。

translations.literal: The regular ritual by which the hundred officials offer birthday felicitations at the coming Tianshen Festival may be suspended.
translations.idiomatic: The regular ritual by which officials offer birthday felicitations at the coming Tianshen Festival is therefore suspended.

sentences.zh: ”至是止 就佛寺啟散祝壽道場，詣閣門或後殿拜表稱賀。

translations.literal: " Thereupon only Buddhist monasteries were used to open and conclude longevity ritual arenas; officials went to the Gate Office or the rear hall to present congratulatory memorials.
translations.idiomatic: " From then on only Buddhist monasteries opened and closed the longevity ritual arenas; officials offered congratulatory memorials at the Gate Office or the rear hall.

sentences.zh: 紹興十三年二月，臣僚奏：“臣聞孝理天下者，帝王之盛德，歸美報上者，臣子之至誠。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirteenth year of Shaoxing, officials memorialized: "Your servant has heard that governing the realm with filial piety is the supreme virtue of emperors and kings, and returning beauty to repay one's superiors is the utmost sincerity of subjects.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Shaoxing 13 (1143), officials memorialized: "We have heard that ruling the realm through filial piety is the supreme virtue of emperors and kings, and repaying one's superiors with praise is the utmost sincerity of subjects.

sentences.zh: 是皆因性自 然，發於觀感，必各盡其至，然後為稱。

translations.literal: All these arise naturally from one's nature, spring from observation and feeling, and each must reach its utmost before they can be called fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Such things arise naturally from character, spring from what one observes and feels, and each must be carried to its fullest before it can be called fitting.

sentences.zh: 恭惟陛下撫艱難之運，憂勤在禦，兢兢業業，圖濟中興，孝德通於神明，皇天為之悔禍，長樂還闕，適當誕節之前，陛下以 天下養，獲伸宮闈上壽之儀，臣民得於觀聽，天下無不欣慶，所以崇大養而成孝理之功者，既以盡善盡美矣。

translations.literal: Respectfully considering that Your Majesty has embraced a time of hardship, is anxious and diligent on the throne, cautious and fearful, striving to achieve restoration, filial virtue penetrating to the spirits, Heaven repenting of calamity, Changle returning to the palace—just before the birthday festival—Your Majesty, nourished by the realm, was able to extend the palace birthday ritual; subjects and people could witness it; none under Heaven failed to rejoice; thus the work of exalting great nourishment and completing the achievement of filial governance has already reached completeness in goodness and beauty.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully consider that Your Majesty has embraced a time of hardship, remains anxious and diligent on the throne, and strives tirelessly for restoration. Filial virtue has moved Heaven itself: Changle has returned to the palace just before the birthday season. Nourished by the realm, Your Majesty could at last perform the palace birthday ritual for all to witness, and none under Heaven failed to rejoice. The work of exalting great nourishment and completing filial governance has already reached its fullest measure.

sentences.zh: 陛下誕聖佳辰，乃臣子所願奉觴上壽，以盡歸美之意， 其可不舉而行之乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty's sacred birthday is the occasion on which subjects wish to present cups and offer long life to fulfill the intent of returning beauty—how can it not be carried out?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's sacred birthday is when subjects wish to raise cups and offer long life to fulfill their duty of praise—how can we not carry this out?

sentences.zh: 臣愚，欲望將來天申節許令有司舉行舊典，至日，百官得以奉萬年之觴，仰祝聖壽，天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Your servant is foolish and desires that at the coming Tianshen Festival the responsible offices be permitted to carry out the old precedents; on the day the hundred officials may present cups of ten thousand years, looking up to wish sacred long life—great fortune for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly ask that at the coming Tianshen Festival the responsible offices be allowed to restore the old precedents so that on the day officials may present cups of ten thousand years and wish Your Majesty long life—a great blessing for the realm.

sentences.zh: ”太常、禮部討論：每遇聖節，樞密院以下先詣 垂拱殿上壽畢，宰臣率百僚於紫宸殿上壽。

translations.literal: " The Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Ministry of Rites deliberated: whenever an imperial birthday occurred, those from the Bureau of Military Affairs and below first went to the Chui'gong Hall to offer birthday felicitations; when finished, the chief ministers led the hundred officials to offer birthday felicitations in the Zichen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: " The Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Ministry of Rites deliberated: on each imperial birthday, officials from the Bureau of Military Affairs and below first offered felicitations in the Chui'gong Hall; when that was finished, chief ministers led the hundred officials to offer felicitations in the Zichen Hall.

sentences.zh: 前一月，分日啟建道場，至前一日，樞密院官滿散依例作齋筵。

translations.literal: One month beforehand, ritual arenas were opened on separate days; on the day before, Bureau of Military Affairs officials held the concluding feast according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: A month in advance ritual arenas were opened on separate days. On the eve of the festival, Bureau of Military Affairs officials held the concluding feast as usual.

sentences.zh: 至日，三省官上壽立班訖，次赴滿散作齋筵。

translations.literal: On the day, officials of the Three Departments finished forming ranks for birthday felicitations, then went to the concluding feast.
translations.idiomatic: On the day itself, officials of the Three Departments completed their birthday formation, then attended the concluding feast.

sentences.zh: 後二日，大 宴於集英殿。

translations.literal: Two days later a great banquet was held in the Jiying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later a grand banquet was held in the Jiying Hall.

sentences.zh: 時命御史台、太常寺修立儀注。

translations.literal: At the time the Censorate and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices were ordered to compile ritual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Censorate and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices were ordered to draft ritual regulations.

sentences.zh: 孝宗隆興元年，太上皇帝天申節，皇帝及宰臣、文武百僚詣德壽宮上壽。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing of Xiaozong, on the Retired Emperor's Tianshen Festival, the emperor together with chief ministers and civil and military officials went to the Deshou Palace to offer birthday felicitations.
translations.idiomatic: In Longxing 1 (1163), on the Retired Emperor's Tianshen Festival, the emperor led chief ministers and civil and military officials to the Deshou Palace to offer birthday felicitations.

sentences.zh: 是日，以欽宗大祥，前一日，皇帝起居如宮中儀，百僚拜表稱賀。

translations.literal: On that day, because it was the great mourning for Emperor Qinzong, on the day before the emperor performed daily salutations according to palace ritual; the hundred officials presented congratulatory memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Because it was the great mourning for Emperor Qinzong, on the day before the emperor performed palace salutations as usual while officials presented congratulatory memorials.

sentences.zh: 乾道八年，立皇太子，皇帝率皇太子及文武百僚詣德壽宮上壽。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Qiandao, when the heir apparent was established, the emperor led the heir apparent and civil and military officials to the Deshou Palace to offer birthday felicitations.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiandao 8 (1172), when the heir apparent was established, the emperor led the heir apparent and civil and military officials to the Deshou Palace to offer birthday felicitations.

sentences.zh: 前期，儀鸞司陳設德壽宮殿門之內外，設御坐於殿上當中南向，設大次於德壽宮門內南向，小次於 殿東廊西向，設皇帝褥位二：一於御坐東南，西向；

translations.literal: Beforehand, the Directorate of Imperial Insignia arranged settings inside and outside the Deshou Palace gates; an imperial seat was set on the hall facing south at the center; a great secondary seat south-facing inside the Deshou Palace gate; a small secondary seat west-facing in the eastern corridor of the hall; two cushioned seats for the emperor were set—one southeast of the imperial seat facing west;
translations.idiomatic: In advance the Directorate of Imperial Insignia arranged settings inside and outside the Deshou Palace gates: an imperial seat at the center of the hall facing south, a great secondary seat inside the gate facing south, and a small secondary seat in the eastern corridor facing west. Two cushioned seats for the emperor were placed—one southeast of the imperial seat facing west,

sentences.zh: 一於御坐之南，北向。

translations.literal: one south of the imperial seat facing north.
translations.idiomatic: and one south of the imperial seat facing north.

sentences.zh: 尚醞設禦酒尊、酒器於御坐之東，有司又設禦茶床於御坐之西，俱稍北。

translations.literal: The imperial brew office set imperial wine vessels and wine implements east of the imperial seat; the responsible offices also set the imperial tea couch west of the imperial seat, both slightly to the north.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial brew office placed wine vessels east of the imperial seat while other offices set the imperial tea couch slightly north of the west side.

sentences.zh: 其日，文武百僚 內不係從駕者，並先赴德壽宮門外以俟迎駕起居。

translations.literal: On that day, civil and military officials among those not in the imperial procession all first went outside the Deshou Palace gate to await the imperial procession and salutation.
translations.idiomatic: On that day civil and military officials not in the imperial procession first gathered outside the Deshou Palace gate to await the emperor's arrival and salutation.

sentences.zh: 質明，皇帝服靴袍出即御坐，從駕臣僚、禁衛起居如常儀。

translations.literal: At daybreak the emperor, wearing boots and robe, came out and took the imperial seat; close attendants in the procession and the guard performed salutations as in the regular ritual.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak the emperor appeared in boots and robe and took the imperial seat. Attendants in the procession and the guard performed salutations as usual.

sentences.zh: 皇帝降坐，乘輦將至德壽宮，文武百僚迎駕再拜起居 訖，前導官、太常卿、閣門官、太常博士、禮直官先入，詣大次前分左右立定。

translations.literal: The emperor descended, mounted the palanquin, and as he approached the Deshou Palace civil and military officials welcomed the procession, bowed twice, and finished salutations; advance guides, the director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, gate commissioners, court ritual doctors, and ritual officers entered first and stood left and right before the great secondary seat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor descended and mounted his palanquin. As he approached the Deshou Palace, officials welcomed the procession, bowed twice, and completed their salutations. Advance guides, the director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, gate commissioners, ritual doctors, and ritual officers entered first and took their places left and right before the great secondary seat.

sentences.zh: 皇帝降輦入次，御史台、閣門、太常寺分引皇太子並文武百僚入詣殿廷，東西相向立 定，前導官導皇帝入小次，簾降。

translations.literal: The emperor descended from the palanquin and entered the secondary seat; the Censorate, Gate Office, and Court of Imperial Sacrifices led the heir apparent and civil and military officials into the hall courtyard to stand facing each other east and west; advance guides led the emperor into the small secondary seat and the curtain was lowered.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor alighted and entered the secondary seat. The Censorate, Gate Office, and Court of Imperial Sacrifices led the heir apparent and officials into the courtyard to stand east and west facing one another. Advance guides led the emperor into the small secondary seat and lowered the curtain.

sentences.zh: 皇太子並文武百僚並橫行北向立。

translations.literal: The heir apparent and civil and military officials all stood in horizontal formation facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent and civil and military officials all stood in horizontal formation facing north.

sentences.zh: 太上皇帝出宮升御坐，鳴鞭，小次簾卷。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor came out of the palace, ascended, and took the imperial seat; the whip sounded; the curtain of the small secondary seat was raised.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor emerged, ascended, and took the imperial seat. The whip sounded and the curtain of the small secondary seat was raised.

sentences.zh: 前導官導皇帝升殿東階，詣殿折檻前北向褥位，再拜， 躬奏聖躬萬福，再拜，皇帝詣太上皇帝御坐之東褥位西向立，前導官於殿上隨地之宜立。

translations.literal: Advance guides led the emperor up the eastern steps of the hall to the cushioned place north-facing before the balustrade; he bowed twice, bowed and reported ten thousand blessings of body, bowed twice again; the emperor went to the cushioned place west-facing east of the Retired Emperor's seat; advance guides stood on the hall wherever the ground permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Advance guides led the emperor up the eastern steps to the cushioned place before the balustrade facing north. He bowed twice, bowed and reported the Retired Emperor's ten thousand blessings of body, and bowed twice again. The emperor then stood west-facing east of the Retired Emperor's seat while advance guides took suitable positions on the dais.

sentences.zh: 次舍人揖皇太子並文武百僚躬，典儀曰“再拜”，讚者承傳，在位官皆再 拜，搢笏舞蹈，又再拜，皇太子不離位，奏聖躬萬福，各再拜，直身，分東西相向立。

translations.literal: Next the usher had the heir apparent and civil and military officials bow; the master of ceremonies said "Bow twice"; the caller transmitted; all officials in attendance bowed twice, inserted their tablets, performed the dance obeisance, and bowed twice again; the heir apparent did not leave his place, reported ten thousand blessings of body, each bowed twice again, straightened up, and divided to stand facing each other east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Next the usher had the heir apparent and officials bow. The master of ceremonies called "Bow twice," the caller transmitted, and all officials bowed twice, inserted their tablets, performed the dance obeisance, and bowed twice again. The heir apparent remained in place, reported ten thousand blessings of body, everyone bowed twice again, straightened, and divided east and west.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引奉盤盞官、受盤盞官、承旨宣答官、奏禮畢官、殿中監、少監升殿。

translations.literal: Ritual officers led the tray-and-cup bearers, cup receivers, order-announcing responders, rite-completion reporters, the director of the palace service, and vice-director up the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers led the tray bearers, cup receivers, order announcers, rite-completion reporters, and the director and vice-director of the palace service onto the hall.

sentences.zh: 內侍進禦茶床，尚醞典禦以盤盞、酒注授殿中監、少監，次禮直官引奉盤盞官詣酒尊所北向，殿中監啟盞，殿中少監注酒，奉盤盞官奉酒詣皇帝前北向，禮直官引受 盤盞官詣太上皇帝御坐前，西向立，皇太子並文武百僚橫行北向立。

translations.literal: Inner attendants brought forward the imperial tea couch; the imperial brew master presented tray, cup, and wine pitcher to the director and vice-director of the palace service; next ritual officers led the tray bearer north-facing to the wine altar; the director opened the cup; the vice-director poured wine; the tray bearer bore wine north-facing before the emperor; ritual officers led the cup receiver west-facing before the Retired Emperor's seat; the heir apparent and civil and military officials stood in horizontal formation facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants brought forward the imperial tea couch. The imperial brew master gave tray, cup, and pitcher to the director and vice-director of the palace service. Ritual officers then led the tray bearer north-facing to the wine altar; the director opened the cup and the vice-director poured. The tray bearer bore wine before the emperor facing north while ritual officers led the cup receiver to stand west-facing before the Retired Emperor. The heir apparent and officials stood in horizontal formation facing north.

sentences.zh: 奉盤盞官躬進皇帝，皇帝奉酒，前導官導皇帝詣太上皇帝御坐前躬進訖，少後，以盤授受盤盞 官。

translations.literal: The tray bearer bowed and presented to the emperor; the emperor bore the wine; advance guides led the emperor before the Retired Emperor's seat to bow and present it; when finished he withdrew slightly and handed the tray to the cup receiver.
translations.idiomatic: The tray bearer bowed and presented wine to the emperor, who bore it forward. Advance guides led him before the Retired Emperor to bow and present it, then withdraw slightly and hand the tray to the cup receiver.

sentences.zh: 前導官導皇帝詣太上御坐前褥位北向俯伏跪，殿下皇太子並百僚皆躬身。

translations.literal: Advance guides led the emperor to the cushioned place north-facing before the Retired Emperor's seat, prostrating himself kneeling; below the hall the heir apparent and hundred officials all bowed.
translations.idiomatic: Advance guides led the emperor to the cushioned place before the Retired Emperor's seat, where he prostrated himself kneeling. Below the hall the heir apparent and all officials bowed.

sentences.zh: 皇帝奏：“臣某謹率文武百僚稽首言：天申令節，臣某與百僚等不勝大慶，謹上千萬歲 壽。

translations.literal: The emperor reported: "Your servant So-and-so respectfully leads the civil and military officials in bowing our heads and saying: On the Tianshen command festival, your servant and the hundred officials cannot contain our great rejoicing and respectfully offer ten thousand myriad years of life.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reported: "Your servant So-and-so respectfully leads the civil and military officials in bowing our heads and saying: On the Tianshen command festival your servant and the hundred officials cannot contain our great rejoicing and respectfully wish ten thousand myriad years of life.

sentences.zh: ”奏訖，伏，興，再拜，在位官皆再拜。

translations.literal: " When the report was finished he prostrated himself, rose, bowed twice; all officials in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " When the report was finished he prostrated himself, rose, and bowed twice; all officials in attendance bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 承旨宣答官宣曰：“得皇帝壽酒，與皇帝並百僚內外同慶。

translations.literal: The order-announcing responder announced: "Having received the emperor's birthday wine, I share this joy with the emperor and the hundred officials inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: The order announcer proclaimed: "Having received the emperor's birthday wine, I share this joy with the emperor and the hundred officials within and without.

sentences.zh: ”皇帝再拜，在位官皆再拜訖，分東西相向立。

translations.literal: " The emperor bowed twice; all officials in attendance bowed twice; then they divided east and west facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor bowed twice and all officials bowed twice, then divided east and west.

sentences.zh: 皇帝詣御坐 東，西向立，奉盤盞官以盤北向恭進，皇帝奉盤，樂作，俟太上皇帝飲酒，皇帝躬接盞訖，皇帝少後，以盤盞授受盤盞官，以授殿中監，各復位立。

translations.literal: The emperor went east of the imperial seat and stood facing west; the tray bearer respectfully presented the tray facing north; the emperor bore the tray; music sounded; waiting until the Retired Emperor finished drinking, the emperor bowed and received the cup; the emperor withdrew slightly afterward and handed tray and cup to the cup receiver, who handed them to the director of the palace service; each returned to place.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went east of the imperial seat and stood facing west. The tray bearer respectfully presented the tray facing north; the emperor received it while music played. When the Retired Emperor finished drinking, the emperor bowed and received the cup, withdrew slightly, and handed tray and cup to the cup receiver and then to the director of the palace service; each returned to position.

sentences.zh: 皇太子並文武百 僚橫行北向，皇帝詣褥位北向再拜，在位官皆再拜。

translations.literal: The heir apparent and civil and military officials stood in horizontal formation facing north; the emperor went to the cushioned place facing north and bowed twice; all officials in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent and officials stood in horizontal formation facing north. The emperor went to the cushioned place facing north and bowed twice; all officials bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 皇帝詣太上御坐東褥位西向立，皇太子、文武百僚再拜，搢笏舞蹈，又再拜訖，內侍舉茶床，奏禮畢官北向俯伏 跪奏：“具官臣某言禮畢。

translations.literal: The emperor went to the cushioned place west-facing east of the Retired Emperor's seat; the heir apparent and civil and military officials bowed twice, inserted tablets, performed the dance obeisance, and bowed twice again; inner attendants raised the tea couch; the rite-completion reporter north-facing prostrated himself kneeling and reported: "The official with full title, your servant, reports that the rites are complete.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to the cushioned place west-facing east of the Retired Emperor. The heir apparent and officials bowed twice, inserted their tablets, performed the dance obeisance, and bowed twice again. Inner attendants raised the tea couch. The rite-completion reporter prostrated himself facing north and reported: "Your servant with full title reports that the rites are complete.

sentences.zh: ”在位官再拜。

translations.literal: " All officials in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " All officials in attendance bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 太上皇帝駕興，皇帝從入，文武百僚以次退。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor's carriage rose; the emperor followed in; civil and military officials withdrew in order.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor's carriage rose; the emperor followed him in; civil and military officials withdrew in order.

sentences.zh: 淳熙二年十一月，詔：“太上皇帝聖壽無疆，新歲七十，以十 一日冬至加上尊號冊寶，十二月十七日立春行慶壽禮。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year of Chunxi, an edict stated: "The Retired Emperor's sacred life is without limit; in the new year he reaches seventy; on the eleventh day, the winter solstice, superior honorific titles and investiture seals will be added; on the seventeenth day of the twelfth month, the beginning of spring, the longevity celebration ritual will be performed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Chunxi 2 (1175) an edict stated: "The Retired Emperor's sacred life knows no limit; in the new year he reaches seventy. On the eleventh day, the winter solstice, superior honorific titles and investiture seals will be added; on the seventeenth day of the twelfth month, the beginning of spring, the longevity celebration ritual will be performed.

sentences.zh: ”是日早，文武百僚並簪花赴文德殿立班，聽宣慶壽赦。

translations.literal: " Early that day civil and military officials all wore floral pins and went to the Wende Hall to form ranks and hear the longevity celebration amnesty proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: " Early that day civil and military officials wore floral pins, went to the Wende Hall to form ranks, and heard the longevity celebration amnesty proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 宣赦訖，從駕至德壽宮行慶壽禮，致詞曰：“皇帝臣 某言：天祐君親，錫茲難老，維春之吉，年德加新。

translations.literal: When the amnesty was finished they followed the procession to the Deshou Palace to perform the longevity celebration ritual, with the address: "The emperor your servant So-and-so says: Heaven protects ruler and parent and bestows difficulty in aging; in the auspiciousness of spring the year's virtue is renewed.
translations.idiomatic: When the amnesty was finished they followed the procession to the Deshou Palace for the longevity celebration, with the address: "The emperor your servant So-and-so says: Heaven protects ruler and parent and grants long life hard to age; in the auspiciousness of spring the year's virtue is renewed.

sentences.zh: 臣某與群臣等不勝大慶，謹上千萬歲壽。

translations.literal: Your servant So-and-so together with the assembled ministers cannot contain our great rejoicing and respectfully offer ten thousand myriad years of life.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant So-and-so together with the assembled ministers cannot contain our great rejoicing and respectfully wish ten thousand myriad years of life.

sentences.zh: ”餘與前上壽儀注同。

translations.literal: " The remainder followed the previous birthday ritual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: " The remainder followed the previous birthday ritual regulations.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，從駕官、應奉官、禁衛等並簪花從駕還 內，文武百僚文德殿拜表稱賀。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished, officials in the imperial procession, attendants, and guards all wore floral pins and followed the procession back within; civil and military officials presented congratulatory memorials at the Wende Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished, officials in the imperial procession, attendants, and guards wore floral pins and followed the emperor back within while civil and military officials presented congratulatory memorials at the Wende Hall.

sentences.zh: 十年十二月，以太上皇后新年七十，詔以立春日行慶賀之禮。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the tenth year, because the Retired Empress would reach seventy in the new year, an edict ordered that congratulatory rites be performed on the day of the beginning of spring.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the tenth year, because the Retired Empress would reach seventy in the new year, an edict ordered congratulatory rites on the day the spring season began.

sentences.zh: 十三年春正月朔，以太上皇帝聖壽八十，帝率群臣詣德壽宮行禮，其儀注、恩赦並如淳熙二年典故。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month in the spring of the thirteenth year, because the Retired Emperor's sacred life reached eighty, the emperor led the assembled ministers to the Deshou Palace to perform the ritual; the ritual regulations and grace amnesty all followed the precedents of the second year of Chunxi.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the first month in the spring of the thirteenth year, when the Retired Emperor's sacred life reached eighty, the emperor led the assembled ministers to the Deshou Palace. The ritual regulations and amnesty followed the Chunxi 2 precedents.

sentences.zh: 孝宗以十月二十二日為會慶節，光宗以九月四日為重明節，寧宗以十月十九日為天祐節、尋改為瑞慶節，理宗以正月五日為天基節，度宗以四月九日為乾會節，瀛國公以九月二十八日為天瑞節。

translations.literal: Xiaozong took the twenty-second day of the tenth month as the Huiqing Festival; Guangzong the fourth day of the ninth month as the Chongming Festival; Ningzong the nineteenth day of the tenth month as the Tianyou Festival, soon changed to the Ruiqing Festival; Lizong the fifth day of the first month as the Tianji Festival; Duzong the ninth day of the fourth month as the Qianhui Festival; the Lord of Ying the twenty-eighth day of the ninth month as the Tianrui Festival.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong's birthday was the Huiqing Festival on the twenty-second day of the tenth month; Guangzong's the Chongming Festival on the fourth day of the ninth month; Ningzong's first the Tianyou Festival on the nineteenth day of the tenth month, later renamed the Ruiqing Festival; Lizong's the Tianji Festival on the fifth day of the first month; Duzong's the Qianhui Festival on the ninth day of the fourth month; and the Lord of Ying's the Tianrui Festival on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 其上壽稱賀之禮，大略皆如天申節儀。

translations.literal: Their rituals of offering birthday felicitations and congratulations largely all followed the Tianshen Festival ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Their birthday felicitations and congratulatory rites largely followed the Tianshen Festival procedure.

sentences.zh: 諸慶節，古無是也，真宗以後始有之。

translations.literal: As for the various celebratory festivals, antiquity had none of these; they began only after Zhenzong.
translations.idiomatic: The various celebratory festivals did not exist in antiquity; they began only after Zhenzong.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年，詔以正月三日天書降日為天慶節，休假五日，兩京諸路州、府、軍、監前七日建道場設醮，斷屠宰；

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, an edict made the day the celestial writings descended on the third day of the first month the Tianqing Festival, with five days of leave; in the two capitals and all circuit prefectures, armies, and supervisory posts, ritual arenas were established and libations performed seven days beforehand, and slaughter was forbidden;
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong Xiangfu 1 (1008) an edict established the Tianqing Festival on the third day of the first month, when the celestial writings descended, with five days of leave. In the two capitals and all circuits, prefectures, armies, and supervisory posts, ritual arenas were opened and libations performed seven days in advance, and slaughter was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 節日， 士庶特令宴樂，京師然燈。

translations.literal: on the festival day commoners were specially permitted feasting and music; the capital lit lamps.
translations.idiomatic: On the festival day commoners were specially permitted feasting and music, and lamps were lit in the capital.

sentences.zh: 又以六月六日為天貺節，京師斷屠宰，百官行香上清宮。

translations.literal: The sixth day of the sixth month was also made the Tiankuang Festival; in the capital slaughter was forbidden and the hundred officials burned incense at the Shangqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth day of the sixth month was also made the Tiankuang Festival. In the capital slaughter was forbidden and officials burned incense at the Shangqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 又以七月一日聖祖降日為先天節，十月二十四日降延恩殿日為降聖節，休假、宴 樂並如天慶節。

translations.literal: The first day of the seventh month, the day the sacred ancestor descended, was made the Xiantian Festival; the twenty-fourth day of the tenth month, the day of descent at the Yan'en Hall, was made the Jiangsheng Festival; leave and feasting with music all followed the Tianqing Festival.
translations.idiomatic: The first day of the seventh month, when the sacred ancestor descended, became the Xiantian Festival, and the twenty-fourth day of the tenth month, the day of descent at the Yan'en Hall, became the Jiangsheng Festival. Leave, feasting, and music all followed the Tianqing Festival.

sentences.zh: 中書、親王、節度、樞密、三司以下至駙馬都尉，詣長春殿進金縷延壽帶、金絲續命縷，上保生壽酒。

translations.literal: The Secretariat, princes, military commissioners, Bureau of Military Affairs, Three Departments, and down to imperial sons-in-law went to the Changchun Hall to present gold-thread longevity belts and gold-thread life-prolonging cords and offer life-preserving birthday wine.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat, princes, military commissioners, Bureau of Military Affairs, Three Departments, and down to imperial sons-in-law went to the Changchun Hall to present gold-thread longevity belts and life-prolonging cords and offer life-preserving birthday wine.

sentences.zh: 改禦崇德殿，賜百官飲，如聖節儀。

translations.literal: The setting was changed to the Chongde Hall and the hundred officials were granted drink, as in the imperial birthday ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The setting was moved to the Chongde Hall, where officials were granted drink as at an imperial birthday.

sentences.zh: 前一日， 以金縷延壽帶、金塗銀結續命縷、緋彩羅延壽帶、彩絲續命縷分賜百官，節日戴以入。

translations.literal: On the day before, gold-thread longevity belts, gold-plated silver knotted life-prolonging cords, crimson silk longevity belts, and colored silk life-prolonging cords were distributed to the hundred officials; on the festival day they wore them when entering.
translations.idiomatic: On the day before, gold-thread longevity belts, gold-plated silver knotted life-prolonging cords, crimson silk longevity belts, and colored silk life-prolonging cords were distributed to officials, who wore them when entering on the festival day.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，宴百官於錫慶院。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished, the hundred officials were banqueted at the Xiqing Court.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished, officials were banqueted at the Xiqing Court.

sentences.zh: 天禧初，詔以大中祥符元年四月一日天書再降內中功 德閣為天禎節，一如天貺節。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxi, an edict made the day the celestial writings descended again within the Merit Hall on the first day of the fourth month in the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu the Tianzhen Festival, exactly like the Tiankuang Festival.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianxi an edict established the Tianzhen Festival on the first day of the fourth month in Dazhong Xiangfu 1, when the celestial writings descended again within the Merit Hall, following the Tiankuang Festival exactly.

sentences.zh: 尋以仁宗嫌名，改為天祺節。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, because of Renzong's taboo name, it was changed to the Tianqi Festival.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter, because of Renzong's taboo name, it was renamed the Tianqi Festival.

sentences.zh: 政和三年十一月五日，以修祀事，天真示見，詔為天應節。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the eleventh month in the third year of Zhenghe, because of repair of sacrificial affairs the Heavenly Truth manifested; it was edicted as the Tianying Festival.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the eleventh month in Zhenghe 3 (1113), while sacrificial repairs were under way the Heavenly Truth manifested and the day was edicted as the Tianying Festival.

sentences.zh: 又以五月十二日祭方丘日為寧貺節，既又以二月十五日太上混元上德皇帝降聖日為真元節，八月九日青華帝君生辰為元成節，正月四日有太祖神禦之州府宮殿行香為開基節，十月二十五日為天符節，皆如天慶節，著為令。

translations.literal: The twelfth day of the fifth month, the day of sacrifice at the Square Mound, was also made the Ningkuang Festival; then the fifteenth day of the second month, the descent day of the Supreme Lord of Mixed Origin and Upper Virtue, was made the Zhenyuan Festival; the ninth day of the eighth month, the birthday of the Blue Flower Sovereign Lord, was made the Yuancheng Festival; the fourth day of the first month, when incense was burned at prefectural palaces with the ancestral spirit tablet of Taizu, was made the Kaiji Festival; the twenty-fifth day of the tenth month was made the Tianfu Festival—all like the Tianqing Festival and entered into statute.
translations.idiomatic: The twelfth day of the fifth month, the day of sacrifice at the Square Mound, became the Ningkuang Festival. The fifteenth day of the second month, the descent day of the Supreme Lord of Mixed Origin and Upper Virtue, became the Zhenyuan Festival; the ninth day of the eighth month, the birthday of the Blue Flower Sovereign Lord, the Yuancheng Festival; the fourth day of the first month, when incense was burned at palaces holding Taizu's spirit tablet, the Kaiji Festival; and the twenty-fifth day of the tenth month the Tianfu Festival—all following the Tianqing Festival and entered into statute.

sentences.zh: 高宗建炎元年十一月五日，詔：“政和以來添置諸節，除開基節外，餘並依祖宗法。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the eleventh month in the first year of Jianyan, Gaozong edicted: "The various festivals added since the Zhenghe period, except the Kaiji Festival, all follow the law of the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the eleventh month in Jianyan 1 (1127), Gaozong edicted: "The various festivals added since the Zhenghe period, except the Kaiji Festival, shall all follow ancestral law.
